These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

   `SessionEnd` hook. Left to the hook, every unattended run would leave no record
   of itself anywhere: not of the skills it loaded, not of the checks that caught
   something, not of how the work actually went, and not of the record you just
   printed. `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE` is what files those logs under the item that
   ran, rather than under nothing.

   It cannot fail your run — the item is already converged and this changes nothing
   on GitHub. If it reports an error, **say so plainly in your final message** and
   end anyway.

## The one standing bound

You execute **this one item and nothing else**. Never list other work items,
never sweep the queue, never act on a second issue in this session — however
obviously stuck another one looks. Recovery is code that runs elsewhere, and a
session that helps out is how one item becomes three duplicate PRs.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	# Growth — discover local packs (per repo)
2	
3	A weekly reflection on **this repo's own** captured knowledge: knowing the Claudinite packs already available to it, notice when project-specific knowledge is worth organizing into a **new local pack** — and author it. A local operation: it writes only the repo's **own** `.claudinite/local/packs/`, landing through a PR **a human reviews** (unlike [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md), which lands unreviewed where the repo's delivery settings allow; the shared canon stays human-gated too — lifting a local pack up is the central promote task's job). 4	
5	There is no windowed Context to bind — the opportunity is standing (knowledge that was never organized into a pack, not a recent change), so examine the repo as it is.
6	
7	This run opens a PR and **never arms auto-merge**. Extract may land unreviewed because it adds prose or a rule to territory a local pack already owns; a **new pack** ships new `.mjs` conformance checks that run at every Stop and in CI the moment it merges — a check can break CI, so it's reviewed, exactly as the sibling [prose-to-checks-sweep](../prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md) is.
8	
9	## Conventions used in this doc

# Working in the canary

This repo is Claudinite's **live canary**. Read this before changing anything here, because the
normal instinct — make the repo green, make the repo useful — is wrong in a specific way.

## The gate this repo is half of

Canon CI can prove a canon change is internally consistent. It cannot prove the change is safe for
**consumers**: the vendored mount, the pack loader, the hook wiring and the skill mounts only meet
a real repo on the other side of a vendor set. So the canon runs
`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml`, which converges *this* repo against a candidate canon ref
and runs the world sweep and the selftest against the result.

The gate's whole value rests on this repo being a **real, disposable member**. Real, or the
rehearsal tests a shape no consumer has. Disposable, or nobody will let the rehearsal converge it.

## What must not be removed

Anything that makes this a member is load-bearing:

- the vendored mount at `.claudinite/shared/` and the `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration
  that names what is vendored;
- the `.claude/settings.json` hook registrations;
- the vendored scheduler workflow, with the repo-hashed cron minute;
- the unfiltered conformance workflow;
- **the `local/canary` pack** — the highest-value shape here. Canon #555 broke the fleet through
  exactly this surface: a local pack's manifest, its rules in both scopes, its bundled skills.

## Reading a red rehearsal

A rehearsal failure is a claim about the **candidate canon ref**, not about this repo. Before
touching anything here, separate the two:

1. **Does the same failure reproduce against canon `main`?** If it does, the canary drifted or
   broke on its own and the candidate ref is exonerated. Re-baseline to `main` and re-run.
2. **Only the candidate ref fails?** That is the signal the gate exists to produce. Fix it in the
   canon. Do not fix it here — a canary patched to stay green is a canary that has stopped
   reporting.
3. **Never quiet a finding with an `accept` entry to get a rehearsal green.** An `accept` is a
   reasoned keep about *this repo's* content; using one to mask a canon regression converts a
   loud failure into a silent one, permanently.

## Repairing the canary

Re-baselining to canon `main` is always the correct repair, and there is no local state here worth
preserving. One caveat, from vendoring's anti-rewind guard (#328): the stamped `ref` in
`.claudinite-checks.json` must be an **ancestor of canon `main`**. Stamp a feature-branch sha and
the repo lands `ref-not-on-trunk`, which convergence then refuses to rewind past — wedging the
repo permanently. Rehearsals may stamp a candidate ref by design; a human repair should not.

Testing repo for Claudinite release tests — the **live canary** for Claudinite's consumer-safety
gate.

Canon CI can show that a Claudinite change is internally consistent. It cannot show the change is
safe for **consumers**: the vendored mount, the pack loader, the hook wiring and the skill mounts
only meet a real repo on the far side of a vendor set. So the canon's `canary-rehearsal.yml`
converges this repo against a candidate ref and asks whether a real member still works.

That makes this repo a deliberate paradox: it must be **real** (a stub proves nothing about
consumers) and **disposable** (nobody would let a rehearsal converge a repo that mattered). It
therefore carries the full member shape and nothing else — no product code:

| Piece | Why it is here |
| --- | --- |
| the vendored mount | the canon snapshot this repo runs from, stamped in the declaration |
| `.claudinite-checks.json` | the pack declaration, the stamp, and the scheduler settings |
| `.claude/settings.json` | the SessionStart / Stop / PreToolUse / SessionEnd hook wiring |
| `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` | the repo's only cron, on its repo-hashed minute |
| `.github/workflows/claudinite-conformance.yml` | the unfiltered world sweep every PR is gated on |
| the `canary` local pack | the shape that broke the fleet in canon #555 |

(Paths under the mount are named in prose rather than linked, because the `claudinite-isolation`
rule bars consumer files from coupling to the vendored canon — and this repo is the last place
that rule should be waived.)

The local pack is the highest-value piece. Its rules are deliberately trivial and deliberately
non-firing: they exist to prove the pack **loaded** — manifest parsed, both rule scopes dispatched,
bundled skill mounted — not to enforce anything about this repo.

Before changing anything here, read the pack's own `canary-role` skill (mounted into every session
here, alongside its `RULES.md`). The short version: a red rehearsal is a claim about the
**candidate canon ref**, not about this repo. Fix it in the canon. A canary patched to stay green
has stopped reporting.

# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`
# lines below, which converge nightly — this file does not, so it must not grow
# logic. It carries no cron; the scheduler workflow's drain is the guaranteed
# delivery and a label event is latency sugar.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      continuation_depth:
        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A backstop against a wedged runner, well clear of any declared
    # `code_work_timeout`; the heartbeat's leash is what bounds real work.
    timeout-minutes: 350
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
          # Every declared task's `required_secrets`, plus the configured endpoint
          # tokens, regenerated by the wiring converge. Actions requires each secret
          # to be named statically, so this list is the whole delivery mechanism; a
          # worker then reads process.env.<NAME>.
          #
          # The converge writes the list directly beneath this line, so it stays last.
          # claudinite:secrets
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor.mjs

  continue-the-chain:
    needs: execute
    if: failure() || cancelled()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Continue the drain, or escalate a chain that keeps dying
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_CONTINUATION_DEPTH: ${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor-continuation.mjs

1	# Publish the Claudinite task dashboard to GitHub Pages.
2	#
3	# SEEDED ONCE, AT ADOPTION, and this repo's from that moment. `.github/workflows/` is
4	# the one directory the nightly update cannot push to — the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is
5	# refused there — so this file arrives with the adopting session and never converges.
6	# That is why it is a thin shim: everything that can be updated lives in the mount, and
7	# only what must be frozen is frozen here.
8	#
9	# The site holds NO repository data. It is a shell that calls the GitHub API from the
10	# viewer's own browser with the viewer's own credential, so publishing it discloses
11	# nothing a viewer could not already read — someone who cannot see a repo sees nothing
12	# of it here. Do not bake API responses into the build; that property is the reason a
13	# public Pages site is a safe host for it.
14	#
15	# Configure it in `.claudinite-checks.json`, on the `claudinite-dashboard` entry's
16	# `config` — not here. Every key is optional.
17	
18	name: Claudinite dashboard
19	
20	on:
21	  push:
22	    branches: [main]
23	    paths:
24	      # The mount is the page's source, so a converge that moves it republishes.
25	      - '.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/**'
26	      - '.claudinite/shared/engine/**'
27	      - '.claudinite-checks.json'
28	      - '.github/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml'
29	  # The push trigger above cannot see the one push that moves the mount most often.
30	  # Claudinite's own update PRs are auto-merged by the Actions token, and a push made
31	  # with `GITHUB_TOKEN` deliberately fires no workflow — so every converge lands
32	  # silently and the site keeps serving whatever the last human merge built.
33	  #
34	  # The catch-up hangs off the scheduler rather than a `cron:` of its own, because the
35	  # vendored scheduler is this repo's one permitted schedule. Following it is not
36	  # competing with it: the cadence stays the scheduler's, and this only asks, each time
37	  # it finishes, whether the page's sources have moved since the last deploy.
38	  workflow_run:
39	    workflows: ['Claudinite scheduler']
40	    types: [completed]
41	  workflow_dispatch:
42	
43	permissions:
44	  contents: read
45	  pages: write
46	  id-token: write
47	
48	# Never two deployments at once, and a superseded build is not worth finishing.
49	concurrency:
50	  group: claudinite-dashboard-pages
51	  cancel-in-progress: true
52	
53	jobs:
54	  build:
55	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
56	    steps:
57	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
58	
59	      # The scheduler finishes every hour, and on almost all of those the page's
60	      # sources are exactly what was deployed last time. A cache entry keyed on those
61	      # sources is the cheapest available answer to "has anything moved": a hit means
62	      # this same tree is already live, and the run stops here. The entry is written
63	      # only once the deploy has succeeded, so a failed one is retried rather than
64	      # recorded as done. A `push` or a hand dispatch skips the question — those are
65	      # asked for, and a forced republish must not be answered with a cache hit.
66	      - name: What the page would be built from
67	        id: sources
68	        run: echo "key=dashboard-deployed-${{ hashFiles('.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/**', '.claudinite/shared/engine/**', '.claudinite-checks.json', '**/*.GENERATED.json') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
69	
70	      - name: Is that already deployed?
71	        id: deployed
72	        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
73	        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
74	        with:
75	          path: .deployed
76	          key: ${{ steps.sources.outputs.key }}
77	          lookup-only: true
78	
79	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
80	        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
81	        with:
82	          node-version: 24
83	
84	      - name: Assemble the site
85	        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
86	        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/build-site.mjs
87	
88	      # The build exits clean with no `_site` when the mount does not yet carry the
89	      # dashboard — adopted, not yet converged. Uploading nothing would fail the run,
90	      # and deploying an empty artifact would replace a working site with a 404.
91	      - name: Is there a site to publish?
92	        id: built
93	        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
94	        run: |
95	          if [ -f _site/index.html ]; then
96	            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
97	          else
98	            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
99	            echo "No _site/index.html — skipping the deploy until the mount carries the dashboard."
100	          fi
101	
102	      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
103	        if: steps.built.outputs.ready == 'true'
104	
105	      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
106	        if: steps.built.outputs.ready == 'true'

108	          path: _site

112	      key: ${{ steps.sources.outputs.key }}

114	  deploy:
115	    needs: build
116	    if: needs.build.outputs.ready == 'true'
117	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
118	    environment:

# Never two deployments at once, and a superseded build is not worth finishing.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-dashboard-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # The scheduler finishes every hour, and on almost all of those the page's
      # sources are exactly what was deployed last time. A cache entry keyed on those
      # sources is the cheapest available answer to "has anything moved": a hit means
      # this same tree is already live, and the run stops here. The entry is written
      # only once the deploy has succeeded, so a failed one is retried rather than
      # recorded as done. A `push` or a hand dispatch skips the question — those are
      # asked for, and a forced republish must not be answered with a cache hit.
      - name: What the page would be built from
        id: sources
        run: echo "key=dashboard-deployed-${{ hashFiles('.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/**', '.claudinite/shared/engine/**', '.claudinite-checks.json', '**/*.GENERATED.json') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Is that already deployed?
        id: deployed
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: .deployed
          key: ${{ steps.sources.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Assemble the site
        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/build-site.mjs

      # The build exits clean with no `_site` when the mount does not yet carry the
      # dashboard — adopted, not yet converged. Uploading nothing would fail the run,
      # and deploying an empty artifact would replace a working site with a 404.
      - name: Is there a site to publish?
        id: built
        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -f _site/index.html ]; then
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No _site/index.html — skipping the deploy until the mount carries the dashboard."
          fi

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
        if: steps.built.outputs.ready == 'true'

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        if: steps.built.outputs.ready == 'true'
        with:
          path: _site

    outputs:
      ready: ${{ steps.built.outputs.ready }}
      key: ${{ steps.sources.outputs.key }}

  deploy:
    needs: build
    if: needs.build.outputs.ready == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

      # Now, and only now, is this tree deployed — which is what the next scheduler
      # wake-up reads to decide it has nothing to do.
      - run: mkdir -p .deployed && echo "${{ github.sha }}" > .deployed/sha
      - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: .deployed
          key: ${{ needs.build.outputs.key }}

name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '12 4,16 * * *'

    inputs:
      wake:

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler-run
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  scheduler-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      pickable: ${{ steps.run.outputs.pickable }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        id: run
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_WAKE: ${{ inputs.wake }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs

  drain:
    needs: scheduler-run
    # An older member workflow maps no such output, and an empty string is not
    # 'true' — so a stale copy keeps dispatching, the previous behavior and safe.
    if: needs.scheduler-run.outputs.pickable == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Start an executor for what this run readied
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/drain-dispatch.mjs

    needs: [scheduler-run, drain]
    # Explicit results rather than `failure()`: `drain` is skipped on a quiet
    # tick, and a bare status function makes this job's fate turn on how the
    # platform propagates a skipped dependency.
    if: >-
      always()

2	//
3	// THE THING IT PROVES. `.github/workflows/` is the one directory the nightly update
4	// can never push to: it commits with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which GitHub refuses
5	// under that path, and the refusal rejects the whole ref rather than the one file. The
6	// pack update flow used to answer that with the WITHHOLD lane — every write bound for
7	// `.github/workflows/` diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, staged into the
8	// maintenance PR as an ordinary added file, with the update ending at `apply-stage` until
9	// a session with an MCP credential moved it into place (#649).
10	//
11	// THAT LANE IS RETIRED (#1317). A member's workflow files are static after adoption, so
12	// no flow computes or stages one, and the probe below therefore exercises a delivery
13	// route that no longer exists. The pack is left in place rather than deleted because
14	// what to do with it is a separate call: nothing depends on it, and a member declaring
15	// it gets an inert workflow and a record that can no longer be delivered by machinery.
16	//
17	// That lane had one exercised caller: the scheduler workflow's own convergence. A
18	// RECORD'S `materialize` shares the same `write`, and had never run against a live
19	// member — which is the residual #649 reopened for. This pack is the thing that makes
20	// it runnable: an inert workflow, delivered to a real repo by the real lane, whose
21	// content the canon then changes so the delivery has to happen again.
22	//
23	// WHY A PACK AND NOT A FIXTURE. The lane's failure mode is precisely what a fixture
24	// cannot see — a token's refusal, on a real push, against a real repository. A hermetic
25	// rehearsal proves the staging directory got a file; only a member proves the file
26	// arrives in `.github/workflows/`. So the probe has to be adoptable content that a
27	// member really declares, and adoptable content in this corpus is a pack.
28	//
29	// OPT-IN, AND EXPECTED NOWHERE BUT THE CANARY. `seededByDefault: false` with no
30	// fingerprint, so `--init` never seeds it and no scan ever suspects it: a repo carries
31	// this only because someone declared it. The canary is the intended and only holder —
32	// it is disposable by construction, which is the whole reason the fleet has one.
33	//

35	// schedule, no push, no pull_request. What is under test is whether the FILE arrives,
36	// not whether it runs, and a probe that consumed a member's Actions minutes on every
37	// push would be paying for an answer it does not need.

40	// ADOPTION — written by the install flow and committed by the adopting session, which
41	// holds a credential the Action token is not. That is the easy half, and it is not the

43	// `materialize` re-vendors the same path through the withhold lane.

46	// and runs no records (`updates/install.mjs`), so a record shipped in the version a repo
47	// adopts at is a record that repo can never reach: `migrationApplies` is `want > have`.
